question.problem: For the function $f(x,y),$ calculate $\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}$ given that $\frac{∂f}{∂y}={y}^{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(1+3xy).$
question.worked_solution:
To find $\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative $\frac{∂f}{∂y}$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{∂f}{∂y}) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({y}^{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(1+3xy)) \\  & =3{y}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(1+3xy)+3x{y}^{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(1+3xy)\end{aligned}
$$

question.knowledge_point: Computing Expressions Involving Second-Order Partial Derivatives
question.worked_solution:
To find ${g}_{xx}(x,y)$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative ${g}_{x}(x,y)$ with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{xx}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({g}_{x}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{2}{2x-y}) \\  & =-\frac{4}{(2x-y)^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

 

To find ${g}_{yy}(x,y)$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative ${g}_{y}(x,y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{yy}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({g}_{y}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(-\frac{1}{2x-y}) \\  & =-\frac{1}{(2x-y)^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Next, we evaluate ${g}_{xx}(x,y)$ and ${g}_{yy}(x,y)$ at $(1,-1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{xx}(1,-1) & =-\frac{4}{(2(1)-(-1))^{2}}=-\frac{4}{9} \\ {g}_{yy}(1,-1) & =-\frac{1}{(2(1)-(-1))^{2}}=-\frac{1}{9}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we have

$$
{g}_{xx}(1,-1)+{g}_{yy}(1,-1)=-\frac{4}{9}-\frac{1}{9}=-\frac{5}{9}.
$$

question.worked_solution:
To find ${f}_{xy}(x,y)$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative ${f}_{x}(x,y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xy}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({f}_{x}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(x\operatorname{cos}⁡({x}^{2}-{y}^{2})) \\  & =x\cdot (-\operatorname{sin}⁡({x}^{2}-{y}^{2})\cdot (-2y)) \\  & =2xy\operatorname{sin}⁡({x}^{2}-{y}^{2})\end{aligned}
$$

To find ${f}_{yx}(x,y)$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative ${f}_{y}(x,y)$ with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{yx}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({f}_{y}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(-y\operatorname{cos}⁡({x}^{2}-{y}^{2})) \\  & =-y(-\operatorname{sin}⁡({x}^{2}-{y}^{2})\cdot 2x) \\  & =2xy\operatorname{sin}⁡({x}^{2}-{y}^{2})\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xy}(x,y)+{f}_{yx}(x,y) & =2xy\operatorname{sin}⁡({x}^{2}-{y}^{2})+2xy\operatorname{sin}⁡({x}^{2}-{y}^{2}) \\  & =4xy\operatorname{sin}⁡({x}^{2}-{y}^{2}).\end{aligned}
$$

$$

Now, we find ${f}_{xx}(x,y,z)$ by differentiating ${f}_{x}(x,y,z)$ with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xx}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({f}_{x}(x,y,z)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(yz\operatorname{cos}⁡(xyz)) \\  & =yz\cdot (-yz\operatorname{sin}⁡(xyz)) \\  & =-{y}^{2}{z}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(xyz)\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find ${f}_{xxz}(x,y,z)$ by differentiating ${f}_{xx}(x,y,z)$ with respect to $z:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xxz}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂z}({f}_{xx}(x,y,z)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂z}(-{y}^{2}{z}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(xyz)) \\  & =-{y}^{2}\frac{∂}{∂z}({z}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(xyz)) \\  & =-{y}^{2}\cdot (2z\operatorname{sin}⁡(xyz)+xy{z}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(xyz)) \\  & =-{y}^{2}z(2\operatorname{sin}⁡(xyz)+xyz\operatorname{cos}⁡(xyz))\end{aligned}
$$

$$
